title: VPC & On-Prem Weekly Handoff Synthesis — Apr 2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a synthesis of the handoff/standup notes from the private deployments squad for the week of 2026-04-06. Focus is on VPC and on-prem installs, customer blockers encountered during late-stage onboarding, and changes to the install playbook that we should roll into the next release candidate. This doc is intended for eng-private-deployments, solutions engineering, and on-call SREs.

Summary (top-line):
- Three customers in late-stage validation; two experiencing production blockers that require engineering fixes (PD-3142, PD-3211).
- Short-term mitigations in place for both customers; longer-term fixes planned and prioritized in sprint planning.
- Playbook updates identified (network preflight, KMS integration checklist, driver compatibility matrix).

Attendees / inputs:
- Maya Benton (owner), Arjun Singh, Casey Liu, Priya Nair, Diego Morales, SE reps from Customer A and Customer B (names withheld). Notes compiled from daily handoffs and the evening on-call log.

Detailed issues and status:
1) PD-3142 — MTU mismatch causing intermittent KV cache corruption
- Observed: Customer A reported degraded latency and sporadic generation errors under sustained load. Repro locally when MTU set to 1500 vs 9000 on their internal overlay.
- Root cause hypothesis: Large-packet fragmentation on the overlay network is causing partial KV cache RPCs to be dropped; client sees truncated cache context and runtime errors when restoring KV state.
- Immediate mitigation: Enforce MTU 9000 on the redwood node NICs and set the overlay to do path MTU discovery; swapped to hostNetworking mode on one canary node to validate (successful).
- Long-term fix: Add explicit MTU preflight checks to the installer and an automated remediation step that toggles hostNetworking for first-boot validation. Ticket: PD-3142 (priority P1). Owner: Arjun Singh. ETA for patch and installer bump: 2026-04-15.

2) PD-3211 — KMS handshake failures behind restrictive egress policies
- Observed: Customer B is using an internal HSM/KMS reachable only through a proxy with strict ALLOW rules. The private control-plane container failed to perform a multi-step key wrap operation, returning TLS handshake timeouts.
- Root cause: Installer assumed outbound access to specific IP ranges used by our hosted KMS fallback; the customer uses private HSM endpoints with SNI filtering.
- Short-term mitigation: Configured a proxy route for the control plane and added a temporary allowlist; created a static mapping in customer routing to permit HSM hostnames.
- Long-term: Expand our KMS integration tests to include SNI/proxy scenarios and publish a KMS/HSM integration checklist in the playbook (includes sample iptables/proxy config, SNI headers, and HSM cert pinning instructions). Ticket: PD-3211. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA for playbook and e2e tests: 2026-04-22.

3) Driver/Kernel mismatch on quantized runtime (customer C)
- Observed: One on-prem cluster failed during quantized kernel initialization after driver update (NVIDIA driver v533 vs expected v525). Crash stack points to cuBLAS/cuDNN symbol mismatch when loading quantized kernels.
- Mitigation: Rolled the node back to a previously validated AMI (v525 drivers) and pinned driver version in the node pool.
- Action: Add driver-version gating to the installer and surface a warning during preflight when unsupported drivers are detected. Owner: Casey Liu. Ticket created: PD-3250. ETA: 2026-04-19.

Runbook and playbook changes to make now:
- Network preflight: verify MTU, verify overlay path MTU discovery, check for asymmetric routes.
- KMS/HSM playbook: add proxy/SNI examples, alternate auth flows, and a validation script that performs a full key wrap/unwrap cycle.
- Driver matrix: single-source-of-truth doc with tested driver/kernel combinations per GPU family and runtime.
- Canary strategy: include hostNetworking fallback and a traffic mirroring step so SEs can validate with live traffic without impacting production.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Arjun: patch installer to add MTU preflight + hostNetworking canary flag (due 2026-04-15).
- Priya: publish KMS/HSM checklist + add proxy e2e tests to CI (due 2026-04-22).
- Casey: driver-version gating and alerting in preflight (due 2026-04-19).
- Diego: update on-call KB with mitigation steps and a minimal reproducer script for MTU/corruption (due 2026-04-13).
- Maya: prioritize PD-3142/PD-3211 in next sprint planning and coordinate customer communication (update to customers by 2026-04-14).

Risks and unknowns:
- Multiple customers are using bespoke networking stacks; we cannot predict all failure modes. We must invest in broader network test coverage and more exhaustive preflight checks to reduce on-site debug time.
- KMS/HSM permutations are large — we will triage highest-impact patterns first (proxy + SNI, on-prem HSM with cert pinning, and internal-only HSM).

Standup log excerpts (timestamps in UTC):
- 2026-04-09 09:15 — Maya: MTU canary deployed to Customer A; initial metrics show latency normalized.
- 2026-04-10 17:30 — Priya: KMS proxy route created for Customer B; control plane able to wrap keys for 90% of calls, intermittent TLS timeout remains.
- 2026-04-12 11:50 — Casey: Rolled back node pool for Customer C; quant kernel stable on pinned drivers.

Customer comms notes (what to tell customers):
- Be transparent: explain short-term mitigations and expected ETA for permanent fixes.
- Provide a small checklist for field engineers to run before escalating (attach as a one-pager).
- Offer a canary window where SEs can validate changes on mirrored traffic.

Next meeting: Weekly handoff + triage on 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC. Please come prepared with short demos of any reproducer scripts and links to CI runs.

Appendix: quick reproducer commands (internal use)
- MTU test: ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000; run kvcache-load-test.sh --parallel 8 --seq-len 1024
- KMS handshake test: curl --resolve kms.internal:443:10.0.0.5 -kv https://kms.internal/wrapTest
- Driver check: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader

If anything above needs immediate attention, ping #private-deployments (alert channel) and tag owner.

— Maya Benton
